lessons.description: Apply the Luk-Strain/Glassey-Strauss criterion directly to the stated data.

lesson.obstruction: The data class of the problem (E0,B0 in C_b^inf cap L^2) is not contained in H^5, while the Glassey-Strauss criterion in the Luk-Strain formulation assumes H^5 fields; the criterion cannot be invoked as is.
lesson.lesson_statement: Bridge the data class to the Sobolev continuation theorem by changing the fields away from the particles: keep the Coulomb field of the initial density, truncate vector potentials of the divergence-free remainder, and evolve the removed part as a vacuum Maxwell field; finite propagation keeps it out of the particle region on a fixed horizon, so the particle dynamics is unchanged.
lesson.summary_quote: smooth bounded finite-energy fields need not belong to H5 (L67-68, summary narration)
lesson.generality: local to the continuation step; applies to any Sobolev-based continuation criterion used with C_b^inf cap L^2 data
lesson.known_in_literature: Ingredients are standard (finite speed of propagation, Coulomb/Helmholtz splitting, radial-homotopy vector potential A_G(x) = (int_0^1 t G(tx) dt) x x, Kirchhoff formula). The H^5 hypothesis is Luk-Strain 2014 Thm 1.1 and footnote 1 (arXiv version), as the paper notes. No reference is given for the combined construction; it is a routine but careful adaptation.
lesson.correctness: correct (paper Lemma cont:vacuum; eqs cont:coulomb, cont:potential, cont:modified-data, cont:vacuum-vanishing, cont:field-equivalence)
lesson.influence: necessary (all of the paper's Section 'Local theory and continuation for finite-energy fields')
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The summary never mentions (i) that L^2-continuity of the vacuum evolution without square-integrable derivatives needs an approximation argument (paper: mollify, then use unitarity), (ii) that the local existence/uniqueness theory itself must be rebuilt for the stated class (paper: Sobolev local theory + modification + uniqueness), or (iii) that the Coulomb field lies in every H^s even with nonzero total charge. The lesson was relearned/re-audited six times (L90, L105, L116, L144, L179, L206) without a stated new defect, except the f/(4 pi) normalization found at L179-180.
